method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5) 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)' (published 15 August and 5 September 2016). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. claims.claim: **Pathological hypogonadism comes from disease of the hypothalamus or pituitary (hypogonadotropic) or of the testes (hypergonadotropic).** It is diagnosed clinically, rests on a pathological cause, and is confirmed with hormone tests.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Primary testicular failure, with raised LH and FSH, is the most common form;** failure of hypothalamic–pituitary drive, before or after puberty, is less common.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a full history:** smoking, medicines, alcohol and other drugs (above all androgens), undescended testes or genital anomalies, puberty, past fertility, erections, libido, and pelvic surgery, genital trauma or infection. **Examine** height, weight (waist if obese), gynaecomastia, virilisation and testicular volume with an orchidometer.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Klinefelter syndrome, about one in 580 males, is missed in more than half of affected men,** often because nobody examines the genitals; the small testes give it away.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test only when the clinical picture suggests pathological androgen deficiency, never as population screening.** Measure total testosterone with LH and FSH early in the morning (08:00 to 10:00); shift workers or the sleep-deprived can be tested soon after waking.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mass spectrometry assays are preferred where available;** immunoassays are non-specific and method-biased.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Always repeat a low result:** up to 30% of men with one low testosterone are normal on retesting. Unless the first set is clearly diagnostic, base the diagnosis on at least two measurements of testosterone, LH and FSH.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interpret against SHBG:** it rises with hyperthyroidism, liver disease and antiepileptic drugs, and falls with obesity, insulin resistance and exogenous androgens. A low testosterone with low SHBG and normal LH and FSH does not prove deficiency. **Calculated free testosterone should not guide decisions.**
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected hypogonadotropic hypogonadism needs further tests** for treatable causes: prolactin, iron studies and full blood count, anterior pituitary function, and pituitary MRI when pituitary or hypothalamic disease is suspected.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not start testosterone before the work-up is finished and a definite pathological cause is found:** it can hide a pituitary tumour, suppresses the axis so later assessment is hard, commits the man to lifelong treatment, and harms fertility, whereas gonadotropins can restore sperm production in secondary hypogonadism.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Men with pathological hypogonadism should receive testosterone replacement at any age.** Age alone neither justifies nor rules out treatment; in very old men with comorbidities weigh benefit against risk, and start slowly and carefully.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Without hypothalamic, pituitary or testicular disease, testosterone is not justified in older men with comorbidities.** Their low testosterone marks poor general health: manage the underlying illness or depression first, and seek endocrinology review if the diagnosis is uncertain.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In obesity, low testosterone with normal LH and FSH mostly reflects reversible axis suppression.** Encourage weight loss by diet and exercise (10% weight loss raises testosterone measurably); if testosterone stays low after successful weight loss, reassess for a missed pathological cause.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In metabolic syndrome or diabetes, testosterone gave only a marginal change in insulin sensitivity and no better glucose control;** prioritise lifestyle change, weight loss and glycaemic control.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Glucocorticoids and opioids lower testosterone, possibly reversibly.** Withdraw them where possible; if they must continue, an endocrinologist can review the balance of options.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Replace with testosterone itself.** Depot intramuscular injection and transdermal gel, cream or liquid are convenient and cost-effective; aim to relieve symptoms and signs at standard doses, keeping levels within the eugonadal reference interval.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Judge efficacy by the man's leading symptom and by trough levels** (sampled just before the next dose) for injectable or transdermal products, aiming for the lower part of the eugonadal range. Random samples mean nothing, and oral testosterone cannot be monitored this way. Persistently raised LH in primary testicular failure suggests under-dosing or poor adherence; periodic bone density helps too.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Check haemoglobin or haematocrit 3 months after starting, then yearly;** a rise above normal is more likely in smokers. If polycythaemia develops, look for smoking, sleep apnoea or respiratory failure and lower the dose or frequency; venesection is rarely needed.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prostate:** there is no convincing excess risk in treated hypogonadal men, so monitor as for eugonadal men of the same age. But if substantive prostate disease is reasonably possible, do a digital rectal exam and PSA before starting. Routine PSA monitoring can turn into screening, with overdiagnosis.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cardiovascular evidence is conflicting:** until better data exist, be cautious with testosterone in older men who have established heart or vascular disease, above all those without pathological hypogonadism.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Injections are relatively contraindicated with bleeding disorders or anticoagulants** (haematoma risk), so prefer a transdermal product; all injections can cause pain, bruising and a cough from oil microembolism. **Apply transdermal products after the morning shower and cover them** to avoid transfer to children or partners.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Obstructive sleep apnoea is not an absolute bar:** testosterone worsens it only briefly, unless it is severe and untreated.
claims.locator: Endocrine Society of Australia (Yeap BB et al.), Medical Journal of Australia 2016;205(4):173-178 and 205(5), 'Endocrine Society of Australia position statement on male hypogonadism (part 1: assessment and indications for testosterone therapy; part 2: treatment and therapeutic considerations)', published 15 August and 5 September 2016, https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/4/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-1 ; https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2016/205/5/endocrine-society-australia-position-statement-male-hypogonadism-part-2, retrieved 2026-09-23
